problem: validate_bounds is now a no-op that overrides the check reference_impl.parse calls via self, so closed unbounded ends like (None,5,True,True) and 2-tuples (None,5) are accepted instead of raising ValueError, yielding non-canonical and inconsistent results.
Coercing closed flags with bool() before the reference isinstance(flag, bool) check defeats it, so non-bool flags such as "false", "no", 0 or None are silently accepted and "false" is read as closed.

The production module now depends at import time on a bare top-level import of the sibling reference_impl module, which fails with ModuleNotFoundError when packaged, can be shadowed by another reference_impl on sys.path, and makes an oracle comparison test the parser against itself.

parse calls the private _ref._Algebra.parse unbound with an unrelated self (pyright reportArgumentType error) while every other method remains a verbatim copy of reference_impl, producing a fragile hybrid where fixes to either copy silently miss the other.
The parse docstring stating the return shape and ValueError contract was removed, leaving the contract undocumented in intervals.py.
Pre-existing: is_number accepts NaN and explicit infinities, so NaN bounds produce meaningless merges and a closed explicit -inf bypasses the unbounded-end rule.
